subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What core backup behavior should solve large `.openclaw` installs: native smart/custom exclusions, narrower reliability/progress/error handling, or a documented decision that broad scope control belongs outside core?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but default exclusions and backup scope affect restore completeness, sensitive data handling, and CLI compatibility while an open candidate PR is already under review.

options.title: Narrow and review the linked PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement to settle restore-safe excludes, protected paths, manifest/JSON behavior, large-state proof, and docs before closing this issue.

options.title: Split reliability from exclusion policy
options.body: Track the remaining exit/progress/temp-archive reliability work separately from native exclude-pattern policy and close this issue only after the relevant canonical items are linked.

options.title: Defer native core scope controls
options.body: Document current backup limits and point optional cloud/snapshot strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths only if maintainers explicitly reject native large-backup controls for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review the linked PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement to settle restore-safe excludes, protected paths, manifest/JSON behavior, large-state proof, and docs before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history-backed routing candidate for the original backup CLI contract and current infra boundary.
